quotes.text: Consider placing the Express Checkout Element early in your checkout flow
We recommend inserting this messaging in the product details page.
purchase data, customer data, and business data
If you use [Checkout](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout.md), Stripe automatically handles passing line items on your behalf.
The Klarna integration for Stripe doesn’t require passing a customer

old_evidence.text: purchase data, customer data, and merchant data
you can optionally pass this data to help improve Klarna’s customer fraud score
line items also help reduce disputes where customers don’t recognize their purchase

findings: The November and May captures have the same core recommendations: consider Klarna in Express Checkout Element early, use Payment Method Messaging Element on product details, share relevant cart line items, and optionally share shipping/billing data (old raw lines 10-32; new raw lines 11-33). These are conversion/underwriting recommendations, not promises of specific offer eligibility, conversion lift or payment success.

The only textual content change in the diff is underwriting inputs described as 'business data' rather than 'merchant data' (diff lines 3-10; old raw line 20; new raw line 21); heading whitespace is presentational (diff lines 12-13). Neither wording supplies a new required field, data schema, merchant/connected-account identity, or changed approval rule.

Klarna's offer decision is described as using a combination of purchase, customer and business data among other factors, with interest-bearing or 0%-interest installment offers conditional on underwriting (new raw lines 19-23). More relevant data can increase chances of higher converting offers such as Pay in 4, but the guide gives no guarantee of a particular offer or fraud outcome.

Payment line items describe cart contents and may help recognition/disputes; Checkout automatically passes them on the merchant's behalf (new raw lines 25-29). This is a Checkout-specific data-sharing claim, not an instruction to duplicate line-item submission or proof that a dispute will be prevented.

The guide explicitly says Stripe's Klarna integration does not require customer shipping or billing objects, but they can optionally be passed to help improve fraud scoring and Klarna might cross-reference addresses (old raw lines 30-32; new raw lines 31-33). Current source line 20 says addresses 'improves' the fraud score categorically, stronger than the conditional source; correct to 'may help' with no guarantee.

Current source lines 13-20 cover all four recommendations but cite only the May capture (source lines 4-7, 22-24). Add November provenance without implying new substantive behavior. Its one-click and conversion language should remain recommendations/availability in the guide, subject to buyer and use-case eligibility noted in the Klarna concept (wiki/concepts/stripe-klarna.md:10-12).
substantive_changes: No substantive integration, eligibility, data-requiredness, payment or underwriting change is established; 'merchant data' to 'business data' is terminology within the same three-factor description (old raw line 20; new raw line 21), and heading whitespace is cosmetic (diff lines 3-16).

A baseline source wording correction is separate from the raw delta: source line 20 asserts a definite fraud-score improvement where both captures say optional address data can help and may be cross-referenced (old raw line 32; new raw line 33).
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 6, 2026 capture recommends early Express Checkout Element placement and product-page Payment Method Messaging; November 7 repeats this advice (old raw lines 10-16; new raw lines 11-17).

May and November guides say offer models consider purchase/customer/merchant-or-business data and that sharing relevant data may improve chances of Pay in 4 or other offers, without guaranteed availability (old raw lines 18-22; new raw lines 19-23).
Both captures say Checkout passes line items automatically and customer shipping/billing objects are optional, with potential fraud-score benefit (old raw lines 24-32; new raw lines 25-33).
conflicts: Source-stripe-klarna-best-practices.md:20 says optional addresses 'improves' Klarna fraud scoring, while old raw line 32 and new raw line 33 say addresses can help and Klarna might cross-reference them. Qualify the source's outcome claim; the related Klarna concept already cautions that buyer options vary by country/use case (wiki/concepts/stripe-klarna.md:10-12).
unresolved_questions: No pinned capture quantifies an effect size, proves a particular Klarna offer or buyer eligibility, or confirms an actual payment, underwriting or dispute outcome. The linked product and line-item guides are navigation only here.

findings: Add November 7 raw provenance, preserving May 6 as historical and noting the merchant-data to business-data wording change without a fabricated requiredness change (source lines 4-7, 22-24; old raw line 20; new raw line 21).
Qualify source line 20: address objects are optional and may help fraud scoring, not a guaranteed improvement (old raw line 32; new raw line 33).

Keep recommendations, Checkout-specific line-item passing, and conditional Klarna offer language scoped as advice rather than proved conversion or eligibility (source lines 13-20; new raw lines 11-33).
conflicts: Source line 20 states a definite fraud-scoring improvement, whereas both raw captures say optional address data may help.
source_assessments.reason: The raw delta is terminological, but the current source has a material outcome overstatement and lacks the November capture's provenance.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna/best-practices, new raw lines 5-33 document Stripe's recommendations to place Klarna's Express Checkout Element early, show Payment Method Messaging on product pages, pass relevant cart line items, and optionally pass shipping and billing objects. Klarna's underwriting considers purchase, customer and business data among other factors; offers such as Pay in 4 remain conditional. Checkout passes line items on the merchant's behalf, while address objects are not required. The May guide, old raw lines 4-32, says the same apart from 'merchant data' wording. The mapped source-stripe-klarna-best-practices.md captures the recommendations but source line 20 overstates optional address data as definitely improving fraud scoring.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/klarna/best-practices, new raw lines 19-33 change 'merchant data' to 'business data' and heading whitespace; the diff establishes no new required field, offer decision rule or payment outcome versus old raw lines 18-32. Preserve May recommendations as dated and add November provenance. In source-stripe-klarna-best-practices.md, source line 20 needs a reciprocal qualification: addresses are optional and may help Klarna fraud scoring, rather than certainly improve it. Express Checkout placement, product-page messaging and line-item sharing are advice; Checkout's automatic line-item passing is route-specific. One-click presentation, request data, or an underwriting chance does not prove buyer eligibility, offer availability, conversion lift, dispute avoidance, or payment success.
